Data.title: Ripple’s Valuation Skyrockets by 400% as $28 XRP Forecast by Standard Chartered Gains Attention
Data.body: Ripple’s $50B Valuation Fuels XRP Optimism as Standard Chartered Sticks to $28 Target Ripple's private market valuation has surged to an estimated $50 billion, representing a 400% increase from roughly $10 billion in 2019. As highlighted by market analyst Diana, the milestone coincides with Ripple's $750 million share buyback, allowing employees and early investors to sell shares back to the company at its new valuation. The achievement is particularly notable given Ripple's years-long legal battle with the U.S. SEC. Instead of slowing its expansion, Ripple continued to strengthen its global position by securing regulatory licenses, launching the RLUSD stablecoin, expanding its digital asset custody business, and completing strategic acquisitions that enhanced its enterprise payments and tokenization offerings. While Ripple's valuation does not directly determine XRP's price, the two remain closely linked. A more valuable and well-capitalized Ripple is better positioned to accelerate XRP Ledger development, expand RLUSD adoption , scale institutional payment infrastructure, and attract banks, asset managers, and payment providers, all factors that could drive long-term demand for XRP. Is the Sky the Limit for XRP? More notably, XRP’s institutional optimism is echoed in Standard Chartered's latest long-term cryptocurrency outlook. Although the bank trimmed some of its short-term forecasts, it reaffirmed its 2030 price targets of $28 for XRP, $500,000 for Bitcoin, $40,000 for Ethereum, and $2,000 for Solana, signaling continued confidence in the long-term growth of digital assets. The significance of that forecast extends beyond the numbers. As one of the world's leading international banking groups, Standard Chartered's decision to maintain a $28 XRP target suggests it still views XRP as a major beneficiary of the rapidly expanding markets for cross-border payments, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets. According to CoinCodex, XRP is currently trading at $1.08. A rally to $28 would represent a gain of nearly 2,500%, or about 26x its current price. Reaching that level would likely require broader institutional adoption, increased XRP Ledger usage for tokenization and cross-border settlements, sustained ETF demand, and continued regulatory clarity across key financial markets. Supporting this bullish outlook, on-chain data shows XRP recently recorded the highest average transaction size among major cryptocurrencies, a metric often associated with institutional-scale transfers. Furthermore, Evernorth is reportedly expanding its XRP treasury strategy , further reinforcing the network's growing appeal for enterprise capital movement. Investor conviction also appears to be strengthening. XRP has continued to post significant outflows from Binance, suggesting many holders are moving tokens into self-custody rather than preparing to sell. Meanwhile, U.S. spot XRP ETFs have attracted more than $1.5 billion in cumulative net inflows, reducing available exchange supply while increasing institutional exposure. Is there more than meets the eye? Well, Ripple's $50 billion valuation, Standard Chartered's reaffirmed $28 XRP target, rising institutional transaction activity, expanding corporate treasury adoption, strong ETF inflows, and persistent exchange outflows all point to the same trend: institutional confidence in the Ripple ecosystem continues to build despite short-term market volatility. As a result, these underlying fundamentals suggest that major financial players are increasingly positioning for its long-term role in the evolving digital asset economy.

Data.title: Unlike the FTX collapse, the $89 million Coldcard exploit has investors sending bitcoin back to exchanges
Data.body: The Coldcard vulnerability has smaller bitcoin holders moving funds onto exchanges for safety, according to blockchain analytics firms. This is opposite of the trend seen following the FTX collapse in late 2022.
